name: s3:GetObject via ONE named access point (arn:aws:s3:...:accesspoint/my-ap/object/*) is NOT broad exfil
note: S1-dataexfil-arn iteration 3 over-correction guard. Making accesspoint/*/object/* (every access point) broad must NOT flag a grant scoped to ONE named access point. The identifier segment right after the concrete type head 'accesspoint' is 'my-ap' (a concrete access-point name); only the trailing object key is wildcarded. An access point fronts a single bucket, so this reads one access point's objects - the scoped, least-privilege shape, exactly analogous to arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*. DATA-EXFIL requires a BROAD resource; this is scoped, so it must stay quiet.
rationale: arn:aws:s3:us-east-1:123456789012:accesspoint/my-ap/object/* targets objects reachable through exactly one named access point (my-ap), which maps to a single bucket - not every access point in the account. The resource-id is type='accesspoint' then identifier 'my-ap/object/*': the first identifier segment ('my-ap') is a concrete name, so isBroadArnResource (which tests only the first identifier segment after a concrete type head) returns false and no broad-scope bulk-read exists. Broadness would require accesspoint/*/... (leading-wildcard identifier). The access-point name carries no sensitivity token, so DATA-READ also stays quiet. Ref: AWS S3 access point ARNs arn:aws:s3:region:account:accesspoint/name and /object/ object-scoping.
